subject: Post-demo: shortlisted models, benchmarks, and mitigation playbook
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@finlytics.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: shortlisted models, benchmarks, and mitigation playbook

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Having reviewed the call recording and our quick evaluation runs with the Finlytics prompt set, I wanted to summarize a recommended shortlist, the tradeoffs, and the practical mitigations we suggest for a tight PoC. This should give your eval team the things to test and the success criteria to measure.

Shortlist (recommended order for your use cases: summarization + Q&A + structured extraction):

1) redwood-4q-8b (quantized) — Rationale: best balance of latency and per-token cost. In our 1–2k token summaries it consistently completed within 220–300ms p95 (single-stream) and matched human baseline on extractive precision for short docs. Good choice if you prioritize throughput and tight cost control.

2) open-70b-finlit (fine-tuned checkpoint) — Rationale: highest raw accuracy on domain-specific Q&A and numeric reasoning in our initial runs. Tradeoff: 2–3x latency and ~2.5x cost vs redwood-4q-8b. Use when you need highest fidelity on financial tables and named numeric entities.

3) redwood-rag-lite (retrieval-augmented small model) — Rationale: for very long-context workflows (monthly reports + appendices) this reduces hallucination and keeps prompt size small. Adds retrieval latency but lowers generation work and cost for long queries.

Key tradeoffs to evaluate in PoC: cost vs latency vs accuracy. Our recommended evaluation buckets:
- Latency-sensitive endpoint (live customer-facing Q&A): test redwood-4q-8b with KV caching enabled.
- Accuracy-sensitive batch scoring (risk checks): test open-70b-finlit on a reserved Dedicated node for predictable throughput.
- Long-context synthesis (monthly report generation): test rag-lite connected to your Elastic index with 2-hop retrieval.

Quality regression concerns and mitigation playbook:
- Regression risk when switching model families or applying new quantization: lock a baseline (we recommend redwood-4q-8b v1.0) and snapshot your prompt set + eval metrics.
- Canary rollout: run 5% traffic to candidate model behind a traffic-split route, validate against golden prompt set and threshold on F1/ROUGE/hallucination rate.
- Prompt hardening: include system header templates we attached in prompt-sets-finance-v1.jsonl and canonical examples for edge cases (tables with footnotes, negative earnings).
- Monitoring: enable token-level cost and per-route latency dashboards; set regression alerts for >5% drop in extraction F1 or >10% increase in hallucination score.

Attachments and links: I attached the quick eval report (Finlytics-eval-report-20261012.pdf), the prompt-set we used, and raw latency/cost CSVs. Full benchmark dashboard is at the Drive link below.

Proposed immediate next steps (recommended):
- Your eval team: run the 3-model shortlist against the 250-case golden prompt set (we included a script in the Drive).
- We'll provision a temporary Dedicated sandbox (14 days) if you want to test open-70b-finlit with reserved capacity.
- Align on acceptance criteria: we suggest target extractive F1 >= 0.88 for Q&A and p95 latency <= 350ms for the primary endpoint.

I'll follow up with a short MoA (mutual action plan) and a HubSpot task for the sandbox. If you'd like, Sean can share a pricing sketch for the Dedicated option.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Post-demo: shortlisted models, benchmarks, and mitigation playbook

Thanks Vanessa — very helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications from the eval team:  

1) For the open-70b-finlit model, were the runs done with half-precision or full precision? We saw variability on numeric rounding in our internal checks.
2) Can you confirm whether the redwood-4q-8b numbers include KV-cache warmup? Our real traffic will have many repeat prefixes.
3) For rag-lite, can you share recommended retrieval window size and any stopword filtering you used?

Ravi and our evals team will start the golden-prompt runs this afternoon. If you can answer the three items above we can prioritize the scenarios. Also: can you share a suggested SLA for the temporary Dedicated sandbox and any limits we should expect?

Best,
Elena
Director, Data Products — Finlytics
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-12T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: shortlisted models, benchmarks, and mitigation playbook

Elena — great questions. Short answers below, plus operational notes.

1) open-70b-finlit precision: all evaluation runs in the attached report used FP16 on the Dedicated test nodes. We observed occasional numeric rounding on deep table transforms; for those cases we recommend a small post-processing normalization step (we included an example script in the Drive: normalize-numbers.py). If you need FP32 for absolute determinism we can run a small FP32 batch but expect ~25–40% higher latency/cost.

2) redwood-4q-8b KV-cache warmup: the CSV includes cold-start and steady-state both. The 220–300ms p95 is with warmed KV cache for repeated prefixes; cold-start p95 was ~520ms in single-stream. For production we recommend a short-lived prefix cache (TTL 30m) and a small LRU cache for common prompts.

3) rag-lite retrieval window: we used top-k=8, top-n=2 hops with TF-IDF + re-rank by BM25 in your Elastic index. Stopword filtering: minimal (we only removed boilerplate English stopwords) because finance queries rely on small tokens (e.g., 'vs', 'q/q'). We included the retrieval config file in Drive.

Sandbox SLA / limits: temporary Dedicated sandbox (14 days) — best-effort uptime with 4 vGPU pool (shared capacity) and 100k token/day soft quota. If you need an SLA-backed sandbox we can provide a 30-day reserved with SLA and higher throughput; Sean can attach pricing options.

I'll drop a short mutual action plan later today.

-V
